content.user_title: Sync ClickUp Roadmaps with Local Planning
content.value_statement: Local roadmaps and ClickUp tasks can drift when teams update both places. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through mapping, syncing, and conflict handling.
actual_capabilities: Maps local epics to ClickUp Epic tasks and milestones to subtasks.
Maps planned, in-progress, and done statuses to ClickUp workflow states.
Explains the expected ClickUp configuration file and sync mapping fields.
Lists setup, push, pull, sync, status, link, and unlink commands.
Documents ClickUp MCP installation and OAuth authentication steps.
Defines basic conflict rules for status, points, and title changes.
limitations: It does not include an executable sync implementation.
It requires the official ClickUp MCP and OAuth authentication.
It assumes roadmaps use epics, milestones, and simple status values.
It only documents three conflict resolution fields.

use_cases.title: Prepare Roadmap Sync
use_cases.description: Plan how local epics and milestones should map into ClickUp before pushing updates.

use_cases.title: Review Engineering Changes
use_cases.description: Compare local planning updates with ClickUp task status before a bidirectional sync.

use_cases.title: Set Up ClickUp MCP
use_cases.description: Follow the documented MCP connection and OAuth flow for a workspace integration.

prompt_templates.title: Check Sync Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my roadmap structure and tell me whether it matches this ClickUp mapping. List missing setup steps before I push changes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Safe Push
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a ClickUp push plan for these local epics and milestones. Include dry-run checks, expected mappings, and possible conflicts.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve Sync Conflicts
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these local roadmap notes with ClickUp updates. Recommend which side wins for status, points, and titles.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Sync Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a repeatable workflow for setup, pull, dry-run, push, status review, and manual link cleanup. Include OAuth and mapping checks.

output_examples.input: I have local epics and milestones. Help me prepare a ClickUp sync.
output: Map each local epic to a ClickUp Epic task.
Map each milestone to a subtask under its epic.
Pull remote changes first, then run a dry-run before pushing.

output_examples.input: ClickUp and my local roadmap disagree on status and points.
output: Use the ClickUp status as the current state.
Keep local points as the planning estimate.
Keep local titles unless the team decides otherwise.

output_examples.input: I need to connect Claude Code with ClickUp.
output: Add the official ClickUp MCP endpoint.
Authenticate through the MCP OAuth flow.
Confirm the workspace, space, and epic folder before syncing.

best_practices: Pull ClickUp changes before pushing local roadmap updates.
Use dry-run checks before modifying remote tasks.
Review sync status and manual links after each major update.
anti_patterns: Do not push local changes before checking remote ClickUp updates.
Do not skip OAuth verification for the MCP connection.
Do not assume conflict rules cover every ClickUp field.

faq.question: Does this skill run the ClickUp sync itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides mapping rules, command guidance, and setup instructions for a ClickUp sync workflow.

faq.question: What ClickUp connection does it expect?
faq.answer: It expects the official ClickUp MCP endpoint and OAuth authentication through the MCP command flow.

faq.question: Can it explain the configuration file?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes workspace, space, epic folder, sync mapping, and last sync fields.

faq.question: How are conflicts handled?
faq.answer: The documented rules prefer ClickUp for status and local planning for points and titles.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Is the MCP endpoint hidden?
faq.answer: No. The endpoint is shown directly in the setup instructions for user review.
